children: Nishanth Vasudevan & Reena Zachariah Mumbai: The Securities and Exchange Board of India will seek details from Tata Steel and APL Apollo Tubes on their multipronged deal, after several stakeholders raised corporate governance concerns over the deal structure, said a person close to the development. Separately, APL Apollo's largest institutional shareholders have expressed displeasure over the contours of the deal, arguing that the transaction benefits the outgoing promoter at the expense of minority shareholders, said two people familiar with the matter. "There is a lot of noise about the deal structure.

Sebi will examine the papers as there is also an open offer involved," said the person close to the development. An email sent to Sebi didn't elicit any response. Under the proposed multilayered deal, Tata Steel seeks to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo and sell its steel tubes and colour-coated steel businesses to APL Apollo for 28,000 crore. Institutional investors individually conveyed their concerns to APL Apollo's management, making it clear that they would not support the transaction in its current form, the people said. "One of our biggest concerns is that there is a lot of debt taken for the deal, while the current APL promoter is exiting through this transaction.

That leaves minority shareholders with a heavily indebted company," said a person. During a conference call held soon after the deal announcement, some investors and analysts questioned the merits of the transaction for APL Apollo's minority shareholders and urged the management to reconsider the deal structure. APL Apollo's largest foreign institutional shareholders as of September 30 were New World Fund, Smallcap World Fund, Norway's Government Pension Fund Global and Principal Global Emerging Markets Fund.

Its key domestic institutional shareholders included ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual, DSP Mutual, Franklin Templeton Mutual, Nippon India Mutual and HDFC Life Insurance. Proxy advisory firms Stakeholders Empowerment Services (SES) and Institutional Investor Advisory Services (IiAS) have questioned whether the deal was structured to avoid shareholder approval requirements under related-party transaction (RPT) rules.

The arrangement, announced over November 22 and 23, involves four interconnected transactions that would change the ownership and business structure of APL Apollo and give Tata Steel a larger presence in the downstream steel market. The acquisition is proposed to be carried out in tranches. Tata Steel would also make an open offer to acquire an additional 26% stake from APL Apollo's public shareholders at 2,301.40 per share.

If the promoter stake acquisition and the open offer are completed as proposed, Tata Steel's holding in APL Apollo would rise to about 52.38%, giving it control of the company. The Gupta family, which currently promotes APL Apollo, would relinquish its promoter position through the stake sale. Since the announcement of the deal over the weekend, APL Apollo shares have dropped about 30%. "Usually when an acquisition deal happens, it's the target company which is the beneficiary. In this case, it seems like the target company's promoters have benefited but not the minority shareholders," said a senior mutual fund official familiar with the matter.

title: Sebi Likely to Seek Deal Details from Tata Steel and APL Apollo
